children: Palm oil prices ended higher, thanks to strength in soybean oil prices and persistent concern over El Nino affecting long-term output, says David Ng, a trader at Kuala Lumpur-based Iceberg X. The trader sees crude palm oil prices facing resistance at 4,850 ringgit a ton and finding support at 5,050 ringgit a ton. The Bursa Malaysia Derivatives contract for November delivery ended MYR79 higher at MYR4,973 a ton. (jiahui.huang@wsj.com; @ivy_jiahuihuang)
